title: Core: Testing Module UI
body:
Closes #29096

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

## What I did

This implements the UI for the Testing Module. It sits docked in the sidebar, floating at the bottom. Notifications were updated to sit in the sidebar as well, just above the Testing Module. The sidebar has a `div#sidebar-bottom` element with some CSS variables attached to allow integrators such as Chromatic to add custom elements here, whilst retaining a consistent UI.

## Greptile Summary

This PR implements the UI for the Testing Module in Storybook, focusing on creating a floating container at the bottom of the sidebar with test provider information and controls.

- Added new TestingModule component in `code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/TestingModule.tsx`
- Updated SidebarBottom component to include TestingModule and notifications
- Implemented collapsible UI with run/stop buttons and error/warning filters
- Added 'runnable' and 'watchable' properties to test provider configuration in `code/addons/test/src/manager.tsx`
- Updated NotificationList and NotificationItem components for improved responsiveness and styling

author: ghengeveld

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Consider using a more descriptive initial state for the description, e.g., 'No tests run yet'
comments.label_reasoning: Suggesting a more descriptive initial state value for clarity of intent.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests a specific change to the initial state description text.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Consider using 'white-space: normal' instead of 'balance' for broader browser support.
comments.label_reasoning: 'white-space: balance' is not widely supported; this is incorrect/risky use of a CSS property.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests replacing 'white-space: balance' with 'white-space: normal' for browser compatibility.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Same as above, 'white-space: balance' may not be supported in all browsers.
comments.label_reasoning: Same as index 1 — 'white-space: balance' browser compatibility issue constitutes API misuse.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Same as above, flags a browser support issue and implies a fix.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Consider using CSS variables for bottom and margin values to improve maintainability
comments.label_reasoning: Suggesting CSS variables for repeated magic values to improve maintainability.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using CSS variables for specific values to improve maintainability.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Remove or comment out this console.log statement before merging to production
comments.label_reasoning: console.log statement left in code is a dead/debug code issue that should be removed before production.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests removal or commenting out of a console.log statement.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: logic: Implement the TODO to clear statuses
comments.label_reasoning: An unimplemented TODO to clear statuses represents missing logic/functionality.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly requests implementing a TODO to clear statuses.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: Consider using a more descriptive ID than 'figure-out-id'
comments.label_reasoning: 'figure-out-id' is a placeholder name that lacks descriptiveness and should be renamed.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests renaming a poorly descriptive ID 'figure-out-id' to something more meaningful.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: The 'as any' type assertion here might be masking a type issue. Consider finding a more type-safe solution.
comments.label_reasoning: 'as any' type assertion may mask underlying type mismatches, potentially hiding real type-safety issues.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a type-safety issue with 'as any' and suggests finding a more type-safe solution.

comments.author: greptile-apps
comments.body: style: The optional chaining and empty object passed to description might not be necessary. Consider simplifying if description is always a function.
comments.label_reasoning: Unnecessary optional chaining and empty object argument add complexity that could be simplified.

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body:
A couple questions:
1 - should we just not render the element at all if description does not exist, or is the element important to always be there?
2 - Can we simplify the API so description can receive no args instead? So we don't have to do `({})`. Unless there are plans to actually populate that arg later.
```suggestion
                      {description && <Description>{description({})}</Description>}
```

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Description is actually required, so should never be null.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests simplifying optional chaining and the empty object argument if description is always a function.

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body: We should probably add a better descriptive classname here
comments.label_reasoning: The classname is not descriptive enough, making the code harder to understand and maintain.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: I think this is legacy. Not sure where it's used but I just left it there.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests adding a more descriptive classname.

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body: what's going on with the 22 at the end? if it's about transparency, can you add a comment?
comments.label_reasoning: The magic value '22' (likely a hex opacity suffix) lacks a comment explaining its purpose.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: Yes this is transparency. Used in a bunch of places, doesn't seem worthy of a comment tbh.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Questions the '22' value and implies a comment should be added to explain it, suggesting a code change.

comments.author: yannbf
comments.body: given you use 500 in many places, can you use a constant so it's easier to maintain and not miss a place when making changes in the future?
comments.label_reasoning: The magic number 500 is repeated in many places; extracting it to a constant reduces duplication and improves maintainability.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests extracting the repeated value 500 into a named constant for maintainability.
